N20x-ocr-contrast-regression.root_cause: Photographed monitors glue W onto PLUS. ContrastStatus.detect() requires a standalone ' W ' token; with the W glued only ' WO ' survives, so a with-and-without study resolved as WITHOUT — 70553 (2.23) became 70551 (1.45), a 0.78 wRVU under-count per affected study. Confirmed by dumping real pipeline output for um-worklist-2837: only row 10 ('MRI BRAIN WPLUS WO CONTRAST') was affected; every correctly-spaced row already resolved.
N20x-ocr-contrast-regression.fix: Isolate PLUS during contrast normalisation so the token boundary is restored whichever side was glued. Modelled against a 12-case battery first: corrects all three glued variants, zero regressions on the nine correct cases.

N36b-specialty-tags-on-device.correction_to_N36: An earlier note said the phone searched only 61 codes and that this was a parity gap against the PWA's 668. Wrong on both counts: the device bundles rvu26a.jsonl (2,164 rows at hcpcs+modifier grain), syncs that table from the same Neon schema, and quick-add already searched all of it. delivery: edge api/v1/reference.js: specialties per code via array_agg, served for every row including untagged ones as []

PAYLOAD_SHAPE token added to the ETag. The hash covers the SOURCE DATA, not the payload shape, so adding a field without bumping it would 304 every device that already held the old ETag — forever, and it would have looked like 'ranking does nothing on my phone' rather than a caching bug
ReferenceSyncClient decodes specialties as optional, so a server predating the field cannot fail the whole sync
code-specialties.json (7 KB, 352 codes) bundled, so a device that has never reached the network ranks identically
N36b-specialty-tags-on-device.the_upgrade_trap: Both delivery paths short-circuit on 'nothing changed': seedIfNeeded only seeds when a system table is ABSENT, so an upgrade keeps rows carrying the empty default; and applyIfChanged returns early when the stored referenceVersion still matches, which adding a payload field does not alter. The feature would have worked on a fresh install and been PERMANENTLY INERT on every phone that already had the app. backfillSpecialtyTagsIfNeeded fixes it: idempotent, stands down the moment any tagged code exists, never overwrites tags a later sync delivered.
N36b-specialty-tags-on-device.found_by: The UI test. Unit tests seed a fresh store, so they structurally cannot see the upgrade path — the simulator still held codes seeded by an older build, which is exactly the user's situation.
N36b-specialty-tags-on-device.model_choice: RVUCode.specialtyTags is a String, not [String]. There is no VersionedSchema and NeuroRVUApp calls fatalError if the store will not open, so the least ambiguous additive change SwiftData can migrate was the right bet on an app already installed on the founder's phone.
